title: Why are you developing?
author: BratPit24
selftext:
I've been using my wives gpt+ subscription to vibe code a game for myself and my friend that we were talking about making since we were kids but we never had neither time not budget to make it ourselves. We maybe had enough skills? We are both developers by training and trade. But neither is explicitly game dev.

Anyway.

I'm getting stopped by the hourly and weekly limit quite regularly. So I was thinking about buying the claude pro licence as its apparently better at the big picture stuff. And it would give me more allowance. But it's 180$ I otherwise wouldn't spend at all.

Which got me thinking.

Why am I even building that game?

It's not for money. God knows nobody cares about yet another ai coded and ai generated assets game in current market.

It's not for the magic of creating process itself. I wouldn't need to vibe for that one. It would be slower but if the process was the goal that's not an issue right?

It's not even about the game itself. I've spent like 4 weeks on it and by now I know that it will never be as good as me and my friend had it in our dreams, but it's been long good enough to just have some common fun and to have something to play along with beer and talk. 

And yet. The compulsion to proceed persists. And every time the model runs out of limit I'm very annoyed that my progress is slowed. Especially since the game got bigger and each new feature eats a bigger chunk of the limit.

I'm kind of beginning to think about as a new reddit/tik tok. A dopamine pump. A fun activity I do after work I can strategise and fantasise, make some notes, and just throw them at ai. And then I see it pop out (almost) instant gratification.

Which basically leads me to conclude I don't want another paid licence. I don't have 180$ to spend on a better tik tok.

How about you. What is your reason WHY you are ai game dev?

comments.author: AdStreet4350
comments.body: Bcz i like playing my idea

replies.author: BratPit24
replies.body: Yeah that's what I'm saying. Basically a toy.

replies.author: FinalBuild2
replies.body: Exactly, lots of hobbies cost way more than 180$. Whatever you enjoy doing is the answer and only you can decide if that enjoyment is worth 180$. Besides, you can just do on and off months, doesn’t need to be a constant subscription and I believe you have cheaper monthly subscriptions too

replies.author: BratPit24
replies.body:
Of course. But when budgeting you gotta know what it is.

 Is it a tool that I need? 
Is it an investment that will pay off? 
Is it a self improvement aid? 
Is it fulfilling a deep psychological need I have in my mind? 

Or 

It's just plain old fun. 

Depending on the answer to the above questions I can spare different amounts of money on that. (I live in a place where 180$ is a solid chunk of money).

comments.author: zeoliteTooth

Later it can be modified, played by your little brother  or even becomes something you did not expect it to become. Who gives a f....just have fun!

At what do you mean become good at? Vibe coding?

I don't think I'm actually growing any skill doing that.

replies.body: There is a skill in using AI. Bur eventually you will nees to learn annd the skills that go into it to understand and craft things properly.

replies.author: FinalBuild2
replies.body:
Not necessarily a skill but ai is a tool and like any other tool, some people do get better at using it than others. Especially if you already have years of game development and actual coding knowledge you will vastly be better than someone who doesn’t. 

Just have fun and you 100% will learn more about game development and using a game engine even if you use ai to help you code (not talking about 1 shot prompting, that clearly doesn’t teach you a lot)

comments.author: count023
comments.body:
I am because it's a game or rather games i have always wanted to play, but due to time limitations (and skills in some place) i couldnt' make them. 

Now i have someone that can build my designs, i can peer review and vet that not only does it play the way i want, but the code is solid and i can release it. It's just another form of creativity outlet like writing or music.

comments.author: Tiscali
comments.body: Cause somebody decided that one of the old turn based strategy games is not good enough for a worthy 3rd installment so I am making a game for myself to play in the evenings.

comments.author: Sedenic
comments.body: This is a very interesting post, thank you for this honest take! It is one of the key aspects that gets brought up in some memes as well... Who are the users of everyone is a creator? It will never be the same experience watching your own movie, reading your own book or playing your own game. It can still be a good experience, but not the same without the exploration and mistery. AI service is a service, which means in order to pay for it, we need to get sufficient value out of it. Sure you can do it for fun, but not everyone has this money to blow on something for fun. Especially if you enjoy other activities requiring money as well.

replies.author: BratPit24
replies.body:
Exactly! I wanted to introspect. I know I'm having fun. But the gpt+ sub I have is for free (my wife got it from work and uses like 2% of it.). So it's no cost fun. But is it 180$ a year fun? 

I don't honestly know.

comments.author: SilliCarl
comments.body:
I've put around 50 hours into my game so far (playing) and have been vibe coding it now for maybe a month? I suspect I'll put another 200 hours into it easily before moving on to the next project.   
Maybe I'll publish one one day if they ever hit my personal standards, which are fairly high.

But its 99.9% because there are certain games that dont exist, that I want to play.

comments.author: SalivaSpittingWorm
comments.body: Because it's something I'd like to play. I tried to learn how to make games before. Before AI. I couldn't wrap my head around coding, and I couldn't remember the steps in Blender. AI has allowed me to do the things I've always wanted to do.

comments.author: crackedpotstudio
comments.body: It’s fun and addictive, I posted my first WIP trailer two days ago and got only 1 upvote and I’am actually happy with that. It means someone liked it enough to upvote it and that is enough for me to keep going.

comments.author: je386
comments.body:
I am a senior fullstack dev for business software and work in that field since more than 25 years.  
Now, code generation comes to play, first with inline code generation, and I created my first game to learn this kind of AI assistance and also kotlin multiplatform (KMP). I open sourced that and put it with the code examples for KMP under the MIT license, so anyone can use the examples, even in business projects.

Then, last year in october, I wanted to learn how to use the new coding agents,  and obviously I could not use a customer project for that, so I imagined a game amd started working on that, first goal was to see if I could do it without seeing the code ar all. It took a week to see it was not possible. But the start was made, I had time, so I continued, and the experiment became a real project, which I released on google play store (android), snap store (linux), as a webapp running on the domain I got there.

I also added a backend for logging and crossplatform saves and community levels and a usermanagement / IAM.

So, this is something between a work pet project to learn and a private hobbyist proect.

Oh  by the way: I often see that I have not learned gamedev and there are many things I do not know from my business software background.

comments.author: DaedalusRaistlin
comments.body:
Because I've had so many game ideas for 20 years and now they don't take months to prototype. 

I was getting by on the normal Claude plan, but I don't think I could go back to it after getting the higher plan. I've still managed to hit my weekly limit a few times. 

Part of it is multiple projects at once. Because I can. An open source project or two, some more work on local tools I'm creating, new rounds of changes for a few games. I could do it all one by one like before on the regular plan, but it would feel so slow. I'd be hitting 5 hour limits constantly regardless. 

I don't need all of the plan, I could get by with something closer to half the price. But they don't offer that, and while I can afford it I'm getting so many personal goals achieved. 

Some of these games even look technologically impressive, like 100,000 units rendered in 3d in the browser in real time. Or the cool city building destruction physics I got implemented recently. Or the game that plays with time scales, walking into smaller buildings and shrinking with them as the outside world moves slower - or the inner ones move faster, it depends on your perspective. 

Cool ideas I struggled to implement before on my own. Feels like I can make anything I can imagine now, so I am. 37 different game prototypes and counting. Different levels of polish and progress, depending on which ones were the most fun to play.
